title: Backlog Horizon Sync — Triage + Prework (Sam)
content:
Context:
This is my personal prep for the cross-functional 60m session on 2026-04-07 with Product, Eng (serving/runtime), and Applied ML. The intent: trim the near-term backlog to a single prioritized horizon of work we can staff this quarter and identify 2 plausible fallbacks if capacity/infra risk materializes. Not a final plan — this is working notes to surface tradeoffs and required inputs before the sync.

Meeting goal (what success looks like):
- Agree on a 6–8 week horizon of 3 primary initiatives (one per lane: product features, infra/perf, quality/regressions) with owners and rough resourcing 
- Capture 3 highest-risk dependencies and concrete mitigation plans 
- Create a one-page follow-up with decisions + owners within 24h

Pre-reads I will bring:
- Short metrics snapshot (token spend, 95p latency, serving availability by model variant) — see linked confluence
- Short write-up on inference infra contention scenarios (PR #218)
- Prompt-eval summary for the two flagged regressions (JIRA: PROD-1293)

Assumptions (call these out in the meeting if anyone disagrees):
1) Dedicated cluster capacity increase request can be approved but earliest delivery is 6 weeks.
2) Quantized model variant reduces cost ~30% but increases 95p latency by ~15–25ms on avg.
3) Product feature A (multi-turn context caching) is high ROI if latency <= 220ms; otherwise impact drops.

Candidate initiatives (short blurbs + rough impact):
A) Context-aware caching (product + runtime) — owner: Maya
   - Goal: reduce per-request token work for multi-turn chat by persistent KV caching and prefix reuse.
   - Expected impact: -20% downstream token cost for chat use-cases; 10–20% p95 latency improvement on heavy-session traffic.
   - Estimated weeks: 6 (1 eng + 1 infra + 0.5 ml)
   - Risk: complex invalidation; needs feature flags and cataloging of pinned prompts

B) Model variant rollout + quantization profile (applied-ml + infra) — owner: Eli
   - Goal: ship 4-bit quantized variant for v2 family, instrument fallbacks.
   - Expected impact: -30% runtime cost, -35% GPU memory; p95 latency up ~15ms.
   - Estimated weeks: 5 (2 ml + 1 infra to validate kernels)
   - Risk: quality regressions on targeted benchmarks; needs eval gating and canary traffic

C) Serving autoscaler tuning + SLO-driven prewarming (serving-runtime) — owner: Jonah
   - Goal: reduce cold-start latency spikes and burst cost by smarter prewarming and TTL tuning.
   - Expected impact: reduce p95 spikes by up to 200ms during ramp; slightly higher baseline infra allocation cost (~+5%).
   - Estimated weeks: 4 (2 infra + 1 SRE), can be fast-followed by ops runbook

Quick triage matrix (Urgency x Impact) — my initial scoring (0–10):
- Context caching: Urgency 6 / Impact 8 => Priority A
- Quantized variant: Urgency 7 / Impact 9 => Priority A
- Autoscaler tuning: Urgency 8 / Impact 6 => Priority A/B depending on risk appetite
- Eval infra reliability fixes (small infra debt): Urgency 5 / Impact 5 => Priority C

Open questions to raise early in the meeting:
- Product: which customer cohorts must we protect for feature A? (enterprise vs PLG)
- Applied ML: what fraction of current traffic is within the quality delta when using 4-bit? Which prompt sets are most fragile?
- Eng/Infra: can we commit a 0.5 FTE for model kernel validation in week 1 if quantization moves forward?

Proposed meeting agenda (60m):
- 0–5m: Quick context & success criteria (me)
- 5–20m: Data snapshot — token spend, p95 by route, top failing evals (Maya/Eli)
- 20–35m: Walkthrough of candidate initiatives and tradeoffs (Maya, Eli, Jonah)
- 35–50m: Rapid triage + vote (impact/urgency) and agree on top-3 horizon
- 50–60m: Owners & immediate next steps; pick 24h follow-up author for one-pager (Sam)

Pre-meeting asks (tiny asks to collaborators):
- Maya: bring exact customer cohort list for chat-heavy accounts (by 04-06 EOD)
- Eli: quick metric on eval fail rate delta at 4-bit quant (by 04-06 EOD)
- Jonah: rough estimate of SLO prewarming ops hours and whether we need temporary capacity (by 04-06 EOD)

Decision nudges (what I'll push for):
1) If quantized eval delta <= 2% on targeted prompts => greenlight A/B parallel work (quant + caching)
2) If quantized delta > 2% but < 6% => prioritize autoscaler tuning + canary quantization on <10% traffic
3) If delta >= 6% => postpone quant work, invest in caching + eval infra until regressions resolved

Follow-ups I will draft during/after the meeting (owner / due):
- One-page commit: chosen horizon + owners + 72h milestones / Sam / due 2026-04-08 12:00
- Canaries + gating checklist template / Eli / due 2026-04-14
- Infra capacity request (SRE ticket + cost delta) / Jonah / due 2026-04-09
- Customer communication draft for enterprise cohort if feature rollout changes / Maya / due 2026-04-10

Notes-to-self for facilitation: keep timeboxing strict, use dot-vote if we diverge more than 10 minutes, call out any gating OKRs early. Capture a neutral record of 'why' we deprioritized items (avoid rehash later).

Quick capture of a few backlog items I want to avoid losing (low priority for horizon but keep on the list):
- Developer CLI improvements for local inference emulation
- Per-route token accounting UI polish
- Minor eval dataset additions for rare languages

Draft one-liner to include in the follow-up one-pager (editable):
"Decision: prioritize quantized variant validation (Eli), context-aware caching (Maya), and SLO-driven autoscaler tuning (Jonah) as the 6–8 week horizon; mitigation and canary gating plans to be produced within 7 days."

End of notes. I'll convert into meeting minutes + actions during/after the sync.
